public_body: West Brookfield Zoning Board Of Appeals
overall: The AG found no violation on public participation and petition refusal, both outside the Law's reach. On the hearing complaint, it could not assess the claim without a recording, but stressed that bodies must ensure deliberations can be heard. No order issued.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board violated the law at its March 13, 2012 meeting by denying members of the public the chance to address the Board.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Law permits the chair of a public body to determine who may address the Board during a meeting, the Chairman of the Board had discretion to deny members of the public the opportunity to speak at the March 13, 2012 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board violated the law by refusing to accept a citizen petition about the proposed solar facility presented during the March 13, 2012 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it refused to accept the petition presented by members of the public at the March 13, 2012 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged attendees could not hear Board deliberations at the crowded March 13, 2012 meeting and the Board did not fix it.
allegations.key_passage: In the absence of any video or audio recording of the meeting, we are unable to assess the validity of this allegation.
